campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered updates to the city's theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for resurfacing work, and the annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27. The Council also considered a budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining equipment or infrastructure, though details on that item were limited in the agenda.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14, the theater use policy, effective September 16th
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, not to exceed $335,000, for resurfacing work
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining equipment or infrastructure

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including meeting minutes, vendor payments, and a conflict-of-interest code update, along with final map approvals for two residential lot splits. The Council also held public hearings on two appeals of Planning Commission decisions involving properties on 6th Street and Oak Place, and discussed law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Appeal of Planning Commission approval for a single-family home and ADU with a setback variance at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of Planning Commission approval of a three-lot subdivision at 14486 Oak Place
Law enforcement service options for the city, ahead of September 19 and September 30 town hall meetings
Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up a routine mix of business, including a wastewater treatment plant agreement, a legal services contract update, and appointments to city commissions and a regional transit board seat. Council also considered a temporary moratorium on new detention or custodial processing facilities in the city.
keyTopics: Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial and custodial-processing facility applications
Jonathan Weinberg's continued service on the Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) Board
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP setting a $21,500 monthly retainer for up to 70 hours

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and the town's monthly financial and investment report for July 2026. The Council also considered several contract-related items, including amendments to service agreements and a heating, ventilation, and air conditioning agreement, plus new professional services agreements.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 Closed Session and regular Town Council meetings
Monthly financial and investment report for July 2026
A second amendment to an existing agreement
A first amendment to a heating, ventilation, and air conditioning services agreement
New professional services agreements for the Town

san-jose.title: San José City Council — September 22, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council considered a mix of financial and administrative items, including reimbursement for capital repairs at SAP Center, citywide insurance renewals, and a funding agreement amendment for a community wireless network with East Side Union High School District. The council also reviewed several city audits, a stormwater management report, and retroactive approvals for community events sponsored by Council Districts 4 and 5.
keyTopics: Reimbursement for approved 2025-2026 capital repairs at SAP Center
Citywide insurance renewals
Funding agreement amendment with East Side Union High School District for a community wireless network
Retroactive approval of Council District 4 and District 5 sponsored community events
City audit reports, including employee turnover and open audit recommendations, plus the annual stormwater management report

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — September 22, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met in closed session to discuss potential litigation involving several fire truck manufacturers and to consider the appointment of a City Attorney. In the regular session, the Council took up a range of items including a solar and battery energy storage project, updates to the historic preservation ordinance and zoning map, adoption of an Active Transportation Plan, and salary adjustments for the City Clerk and City Manager.
keyTopics: Potential legal case involving fire apparatus manufacturers (Pierce, Oshkosh, REV Group, Rosenbauer, and others) and City Attorney appointment discussed in closed session
Professional services agreement for renovations to the Shoreline Athletic Fields
Actions related to the 2000 North Shoreline Boulevard property
Energy services contract for a solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage project
Update to the Historic Preservation Ordinance and Zoning Map, and adoption of the Active Transportation Plan

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 19, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: This was a brief special morning session of the Sunnyvale City Council held for the annual State of the City event. The agenda consisted mainly of the event schedule and standard procedural information for the public.
keyTopics: State of the City special meeting and event schedule

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met to discuss a possible land negotiation for property on Finch Avenue with the Cupertino Union School District, along with anticipated litigation in closed session. In the regular session, the Council considered routine business items including an AI use policy for the Council, a Civil Grand Jury response about pothole damage claims, and appointments to a subcommittee for selecting a future city lobbyist.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of Cupertino High School students for their achievements at the 2026 FBLA National Leadership Conference
Postponement of an ordinance updating building code definitions for 'attic,' 'garages,' and 'square footage' to October 6, 2026
Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy
Approval of a response to the Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims processes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — September 22, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council held a joint meeting with the Stadium Authority Board that began with a closed session covering ongoing litigation involving the DWR, potential new litigation, a possible litigation exposure matter, and a property damage claim from Travelers Insurance. In open session, the Council issued several proclamations and considered contracts for HVAC control systems and office furnishings, while an ordinance on replacement housing unit zoning regulations was deferred to a future meeting.
keyTopics: Closed session on litigation involving Silicon Valley Power/Northern California Power Agency vs. the California Department of Water Resources
Closed session on anticipated litigation and a potential litigation exposure matter, plus a property damage claim from Travelers Insurance
Deferral of an ordinance to establish new zoning regulations (Chapter 18.68) for replacement housing units under state law
Proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month, Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, and Public Power Week
Contracts considered for HVAC control systems (Syserco, Inc.) and office furnishings (D & D Learning Spaces)

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council reviewed a draft plan for how the city will use federal Community Development Block Grant funds, and heard updates on the red light camera traffic safety program and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The Council also took up financial actions related to winding down the former Redevelopment Agency, including a bond refunding resolution.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolutions related to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including sale and issuance of refunding bonds

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — September 17, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Architectural Review Board considered a proposal for 950 Page Mill Road involving a master sign program for a new multi-tenant monument sign. The sign would include branding for the property itself ('Page Mill Labs') along with four separate panels identifying individual tenants.
keyTopics: Master Sign Program proposal for 950 Page Mill Road
Monument sign combining property branding ('Page Mill Labs') with tenant identification
Four tenant identification panels included in the design
Project deemed exempt from CEQA under the accessory structures exemption
Site located in the Research Park (RP) zoning district
